data.title: Play is as it Lays Episode 7: PISCES LOVES VIRGO
data.description:
A set built on the idea that opposites don't meet in the middle — they hold each other in place.
It opens almost still, with Taraneh and Sade, and climbs slowly through Nicolas Jaar and a Soulwax remix of Robyn before settling into a long run of house: Cinthie's unvarnished Berlin functionality sitting next to ANOTR's vocal warmth, Sofia Kourtesis next to Moby and Avalon Emerson. Precision and feeling, trading places.


Tracey Thorn appears twice. Once in the middle, inside a Four Tet production where every element is placed with total control. And again at the very end, singing "Protection" over Massive Attack's dub, where nothing is controlled at all. Same voice, twenty-nine years apart, holding up in both climates.
The set closes in the same key it opened in.

It’s a two-drink minimum tonight, guys, and make sure to tip your mitochondria. You’ve been a great crowd.

data.title: Play is as it Lays Episode 6: LEO ENERGY - SULTRY SUMMER
data.description:
Summer heat. Leo season. The moment when confidence becomes magnetism and the dancefloor becomes your stage.
This set is unapologetic sensuality. It opens sultry—not vulnerable, but assured. Groovy, confident, eyes-on-you energy. The kind of summer where you know exactly what you want and you're not shy about it.

The peak moment is pure self-assurance—you-being-exactly-who-you-are energy. Then it retreats luxuriously through deep house, but never loses heat. Locklead's "Moon" and Montano's "Shadows Don't Lie" keep the sensuality alive as the intensity drops. Close with Madonna & William Orbit's "Erotica"—the ultimate statement: this is mine.

This is Leo energy: hot, theatrical, generous with pleasure, unapologetic about desire. Summer as performance art.

data.title: Play is as it Lays Episode 5: CANCER SEASON SUMMER CLUB ENERGY
data.description:
Summer Solstice. Cancer season. The moment of peak light before the turn inward—and this 17-track set mirrors that exact emotional arc.
It opens vulnerable with Jessie Ware asking "Please" over a Ross from Friends remix—Cancer arriving with their heart already exposed, no pretense. Then it builds a circle: underground club luminaries (TOKIMONSTA, D. Seinfeld, The Martinez Brothers) alongside trusted pop voices (Charli XCX, Madonna). This isn't a climb toward ego; it's a gathering of the real ones, the people worth protecting.

It turns out it's been an entire day out here. Hour by hour, everything accumulates, until eventually the sun is back where it was and the stars are familiar once again. Or... are they? Wasn't that one a little more to the left? Wasn't that one quite a bit brighter? Whatever you call them, whatever they mean to you - the stars are all around us: a dizzying swirl of Japanese math pop, Tunisian hip hop, Polish prog, overtone, lounge, tsapiky, disco... something for everyone!

From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #20
data.description: As is the new custom around these+those parts (all parts of course interchangeable for easy reconfiguration), Axaxaxas Mlö closes out another tentet with a celebration. Yes, yes, they're all celebrations, but in today's world, we'll take any excuse for a party: Moroccan gnawa guitar, Pakistani Sufi flamenco guitar, the smoothest Japanese funk-rock grooves, Philly's finest Anarcho-Christian trance-punk, teenage Māori folk, and more! (Including a lengthy and dramatic appearance from the legendary no-input mixing board).

data.title: Play is as it Lays Episode 3: ARIES SEASON: DANCE AS RESISTANCE
data.description: The first sign. New beginnings. Ruled by Mars, the god of war — this is confident, not combative. Burning bright, not burning down. Bold, energetic, impulsive — 16 tracks of euphoric refusal to let the world dim your light. Dancing as an act of survival. The fight for peace and joy.

data.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #19
data.description: Axaxaxas Mlö is awake and in a good mood. What's our secret? Egypt's hottest club music. Hyperspeed maximalist sensory-overload dance tracks. The long-overdue meeting of overtone singing and beatboxing. All sorts of experimental & traditional pop sounds from just about everywhere. And, of course, MC Hellshit + DJ Carhouse

data.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #18
data.description: Against all some odds, Axaxaxas Mlö is still here - two weeks older but only a week & a half wiser (don't ask). It's a high-energy show this time around: dancehall, punk rock, kwaito, reggae, gqom, and more; with the usual brief detours into those dense & dreamy folky psychedelic fogs that never fully lift 'round these parts. And where will we be next time? Don't worry about it yet, we'll just be there

data.description: We stray from the path so frequently here, in this world. But a path can only lead where others have already led, and leaders frequently disappoint. At least, as they say, all roads lead to Axaxaxas Mlö. And so do playlists, in their way. Let's follow this one, shall we? Deep Korean reggae. Mongolian shaman rock. Ancient wax cylinder flamenco fragments and the world's biggest star, all together at last. Luckily, wherever we end up, we'll meet you there again in a couple of weeks.

data.description: Music is a way through. Not the only way, but it's a big one - and you can clear quite a path. data.description: At last, it's the edition we've all been waiting for since last edition - another hourlong meandering around the vast unknown and in betweens. Safe travels!

data.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #13
data.description: welcome back to axaxaxas mlö, where we're carefully shoveling the last bits of 2025 into the ocean/inland sea/freshwater pond. join us for a sampling of some of our favorite music of the year: from the delightful returns of Noura Mint Seymali and Ata Kak to new discoveries Kasai, Yalla Miku and Ya Tosiba; new music from MC Yallah, Ammar 808, and Keiji Haino. plus, more! start the year off right.

data.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Axaxaxas Mlö #12
data.description:
In this twelfth manifestation of Axaxaxas Mlö, we celebrate the mighty Reissue with some of our favorite new-old music of the year. From the disorientingly slooooow cumbia rebajada of Sonido Dueñez to the sacred and otherworldly begena of Akalu Yossef, with stops along the way for Yat-Kha's Tuvan industrial grooves, the swinging kwaito of Johannesburg's Moskito, and an extended stay in Ghana, Benin and Zimbabwe for a flight of classic highlife & Afro-rock.

data.title: An Evening of Stand-Up Cosmogony, Hour #1
data.description:
the first night begins like any other - until an act of profound nepotism radiates outward amongst the cosmic microwave background murmuration. expansion, once triggered, sets in quickly, to an erratic beat. voices appear and disappear in the murk of a vast precellular sludge.
theories abound that some consciousness, still epochs away, has discovered a means of projecting intention (the strongest force in any universe tbd) backwards, downstream, to the heart of this as-yet-intentionless cosmos. it begins to spin a fiction.

Beyond Karaoke Episode VII - The Zodiac + Other Myths
data.description: Happy New Year! Are you on the edge of your seat wondering what 2021 has in store? Host and KJ K Sera Sarah takes a celestial journey through the zodiac in this episode of mythical proportions! Introducing very special guest and cosmic consultant Aurora Dawn who beams in horoscopes for every sign along the way! Tune in for astrological anthems from The Prodigy, Danzig, Janelle Monae, Throbbing Gristle, and MORE!

data.title: Beyond Karaoke Episode V - Life, Death, & Existential Dread
data.description: Are you ready to stare into the abyss? Host and KJ K Sera Sarah is on a search to find the meaning of life! Let’s peel back the layers of this onion we call existence with the music of Queen, Motorhead, Molly Nilsson, Diamanda Galas, and MORE!

data.title: Beyond Karaoke Episode IV - Diegetic not Diegetic
data.description: Host and KJ K Sera Sarah is getting her kicks above the waistline with a heady brew of musical numbers from stage and film! Using philosophy as our guiding star, we are going to figure out if the voices are real, and if so, where are they coming from? Get ready to act out to songs from the musicals Hair, FAME, The Apple, Hamilton, and MORE! Hail Zeus!
